transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Samir Patel (Vyra - Head of ML), Elena Ruiz (Vyra - Platform Eng), Marcus Lee (Vyra - SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick console walkthrough focused on request-thread mapping and error analysis. Demoed a real example where partial tokenization + KV cache misses caused high tail latency and model fallback to larger variant. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted, SSO, SOC2, and pilot logistics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes, um I'm Jordan with Redwood, AE, and priya who will run the deep dive on the console.
[00:12] Priya: hey hi all, I'll jump in with the Request Thread Mapper — it's the thing that we use to stitch partial requests, kv cache hits, and fallback events into a single timeline. quick note, some of the UI labels might render as K-V cash in the auto transcript, sorry about that.
[00:28] Samir: cool, yeah we saw your deck, our main problem is intermittent 3-5 second spikes on a subset of calls, and we can't really tell if it's model warmup, network, or our prompt truncation.
[00:40] Elena: and to add, we often see partial responses flagged as errors in our logs but the console shows them as okay — so we need better correlation.
[00:50] Marcus: we've also got a migration to a V-P-C in progress, so any plan that requires open traffic will be tricky.
[00:58] Priya: understood. i'll start from the top — here's the request list, you can see each request row has a small thread icon, that expands into the thread view which lines up the client call, route selection, model variant, kv cache hit/miss, and any fallback event.
[01:18] Priya: (screen) so I'm clicking one where time jumped — you'll see a little orange marker at token 24, that's when the runtime triggered a fallback because the quantized variant reported an out-of-vocab or slowed kernel.
[01:32] Jordan: quick interrup — can you show what the original request payload looked like, and where the prefix caching comes in?
[01:38] Priya: yep, there's an export button — here's the client prompt, we also show the prefix hash, the cache lookup result, and the KV cache latency. for this one the cache miss was 32ms but the model variant warmup added 1.9s.
[01:54] Samir: wait 1.9s — is that just model cold start or also serialization?
[02:00] Priya: mostly variant swap and kernel warmup, sometimes it's GPU paging if there's memory pressure. the mapper shows an event 'variant_swap' with a little stack trace.
[02:12] Elena: hmm, do you capture the upstream service call times too? We have a lambda chain we want to correlate.
[02:19] Priya: yes we accept optional trace IDs in the request header and will stitch them, otherwise we heuristically match by client id + timestamp. it's not perfect if clocks skew, but you can upload your trace map and we will correlate.
[02:33] Marcus: is there a retention limit for those stitch maps? our security asks about retention windows.
[02:39] Jordan: we can configure retention per account — default is 90 days for live traces, but enterprise can set custom retention in Private/Dedicated. we'll share SOC2 details shortly.
[02:50] Samir: good. could you show an example where a partial response was misclassified as success and then caused downstream errors?
[02:58] Priya: sure, here's one — the thread view highlights segments: generation, stop token detection, and post-processing. you'll notice the partial response was returned, but the post-processing stage threw an exception; the console flags the final status as 'postproc_error' while the top-level request looked 200.
[03:15] Priya: we also surface the raw response bytes and the parsed JSON — sometimes our tokenizer splits into multi-byte sequences, which the exporter mislabels, so the transcript might show weird punctuation.
[03:29] Elena: ok that's actually helpful, because our own logs only have the 200 but no body content due to redaction. how do you handle PII?
[03:36] Jordan: we support on-request redaction hooks and customer-side masking, plus KMS integration for encryption at rest in Private installs. we'll send over the KMS/HSM doc.
[03:46] Samir: and SSO? we use Okta and need SCIM and SAML.
[03:50] Jordan: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported, role-based access control is in the console — we'll include the SSO pack.
[03:57] Marcus: back to the trace, can the mapper show multiple fallbacks in one request? we've seen chains where it falls to smaller quantized variant then back to larger model.
[04:05] Priya: yes, the timeline is event-stream based — each event has type, candidate_model, reason code. you can filter to 'fallback' and see sequence of model candidates with timestamps.
[04:18] Priya: here's another interesting case — kv cache thrashing. the thread shows repeated cache evict/invalidate events caused by a long prefix churn. the console suggests a caching window change or pinning certain prefixes.
[04:33] Elena: do you have automated suggestions? like Optimize suggestions for batch sizes or quantization?
[04:37] Priya: the Optimize tab will suggest batch targets, quantization profiles, and cache TTL adjustments based on observed distributions. in the request thread view we show the suggestion confidence.
[04:48] Samir: confidence scoring is important — can we map suggestions to cost delta estimates?
[04:52] Jordan: yes, we show estimated token cost delta and p50/p95 latency impact. it's a modeling estimate but usually within 10-15% in our benchmarks.
[05:03] Marcus: I want to surface a specific failure pattern — user prompts with embedded JSON arrays that blow up the tokenization. will console show tokenizer diagnostics?
[05:11] Priya: we have a tokenizer debug trace: token boundaries, byte offsets, and where tokenization differs across variants. you can export diffs.
[05:20] Elena: nice. about observability — do you emit spans to our existing tracing backend? Jaeger/Tempo?
[05:26] Priya: we emit OpenTelemetry spans and can ship to your collector. if you give us trace_export credentials, we can auto-forward.
[05:34] Samir: what's the onboarding flow for a quick POC — we want to run a 2-week pilot on a subset of calls to validate tail reduction.
[05:41] Jordan: standard POC: share sample logs, we onboard into a sandbox account, instrument a subset of traffic via simple SDK or reverse proxy, run a week of traces, then review the Optimize suggestions and run a canary. timeline ~2–3 weeks to initial data.
[05:55] Samir: sounds fine. cost of the sandbox?
[05:58] Jordan: sandbox is free for 30 days for this pilot; post-pilot we'd propose a short Dedicated commit if you want predictable latency.
[06:07] Marcus: on Dedicated vs Hosted — with our VPC setup, is traffic egress going out of our subnet?
[06:12] Priya: in Private/Dedicated, the control plane can be customer-managed; data-plane stays within your VPC if you choose the private deployment — no public egress.
[06:21] Elena: good. can we see an example alert rule — p95 token latency > 2s?
[06:26] Priya: yes, we have built-in alert templates; you can export to PagerDuty or Slack and include a deep link into the thread so engineers can click through from the alert to the exact token where the fallback triggered.
[06:40] Samir: demo the deep link please.
[06:42] Priya: clicking alert — opens thread, highlights the event, shows the stack and raw response. here's a share link — note: link permissions inherit RBAC.
[06:55] Marcus: what about request sampling? we can't send everything due to cost.
[06:59] Priya: we support rule-based sampling, prefix-based retention, and include-based capture (e.g., sample only requests with status != 200 or size > X). also pre-scrub PII via regex filters.
[07:14] Elena: the team wants to run our own bench against you — we have a micro-benchmark harness, can we run direct API calls to hosted and measure?
[07:21] Jordan: absolutely, we can provide an endpoint and a benchmark spec. we usually recommend 3x runs at p50/p95 and a 30-minute sustained run to measure autoscaling behavior.
[07:32] Priya: and if you'd like, we can run a guided benchmark and share the spreadsheet with cost breakdowns, token counts, and inferred per-token micro-latency.
[07:42] Samir: ok let's do that.
[07:44] — brief pause while screenshare transitions —
[08:05] Priya: i'm jumping into the logs view now — top right you can toggle 'stitch mode' which merges raw logs and traces, and here you can see the raw request body, headers, response, and a mini timeline.
[08:22] Priya: note the 'heuristic timestamp adjust' — if your client times are off, we shift them up to 200ms to line up events, but we annotate that's an adjusted time.
[08:35] Marcus: is that adjustment audited? we need to prove no tampering.
[08:39] Jordan: yes adjustments are flagged and immutable — the platform keeps original and adjusted timestamps in the audit log. enterprise controls allow turning adjustments off.
[08:50] Elena: we've had a customer question: can we redact request bodies post-ingest?
[08:54] Priya: yes, the console has a redact-on-demand option — you can submit a redact request and the system will remove the payload from live indices and mark the trace as redacted. we keep a sealed copy in an encrypted vault if you opt-in for legal reasons.
[09:09] Samir: switching gears, any known gotchas for our language-family? we do biomedical Q/A often.
[09:15] Priya: longer context can cause kv cache thrash — recommendation is to pin common prefixes and use chunked retrieval. optimize recommendations will flag high prefix churn. also watch quantized variant lower vocab coverage — you'll see higher fallback rates.
[09:30] Marcus: what do fallback reason codes look like? are they numeric?
[09:34] Priya: they're human readable and machine codes — e.g., FALLBACK_REASON_QUANT_VOCAB, FALLBACK_REASON_OOM, FALLBACK_REASON_LATENCY_THRESHOLD. you can filter by code.
[09:47] Jordan: can i ask, do you have a preferred SLA for p95?
[09:50] Samir: we're targeting p95 < 700ms for typical prompts, with spikes tolerated up to 1.5s for edge cases.
[09:58] Priya: noted. we can architect a Dedicated lane with warmed model pools and pre-pinned KV caches to meet that.
[10:06] Elena: we have a compliance review next week — if we put Redwood behind our VPC, what audit logs do you provide?
[10:11] Jordan: access audit logs, role changes, and full request trace audit trails; logs can be shipped to your SIEM or stored in our encrypted blob with customer-managed keys.
[10:22] Samir: any customers in healthcare? data residency concerns.
[10:26] Jordan: yes, several — we'll share anonymized case studies; Private on-prem option is available for PHI workloads.
[10:35] Marcus: circling back to the tokenizer issue — can we get a dump of token diffs for a sample set?
[10:40] Priya: yes, please upload 10-20 representative requests and we'll return tokenization diffs and a recommendation doc.
[10:48] Elena: ok i'll put that in the action items.
[10:51] Jordan: cool. next i want to show the playback feature — which replays a request through the runtime in a sandbox, showing exact timings including batch queuing and kernel exec time.
[11:03] Priya: playback is great for repro — you can toggle candidate models and see how latency changes, and create a synthetic trace.
[11:12] Samir: is playback deterministic? will it always hit the same path?
[11:16] Priya: mostly deterministic for stateless calls, but for caching behavior you can choose to flush caches before playback. also note that variability from multi-tenant GPUs may still introduce noise; for that we recommend Dedicated runs.
[11:29] Marcus: is there a way to replay at scale? we want to run 1,000 replays overnight.
[11:34] Priya: yes there's an async replay queue and you can export results. if you want production-equivalent throughput, we do recommend scheduling a dedicated capacity window.
[11:45] Elena: any limits on request body sizes for trace capture?
[11:49] Priya: defaults are 1MB per request captured, larger can be configured for enterprise.
[11:55] Samir: OK — how do we get you our sample logs? Elena will upload to a secure S3 with temporary creds?
[12:02] Jordan: yes we prefer a secure S3 upload; we'll hand you a signed URL or you can use our uploader script which strips PII on the client side.
[12:12] Elena: perfect.
[12:15] Priya: the last part i'll demo is the error analysis heatmap — it aggregates by error codes, model variants, and prefixes. clicking a cell jumps you to a representative thread.
[12:27] Priya: for this account you can set grouping keys — by prompt template id, by user cohort, or by endpoint.
[12:36] Marcus: do you have programmatic access to that heatmap? we want to pull it into our internal dashboards.
[12:41] Priya: yes the Console has an API to query aggregated metrics and export CSVs.
[12:47] Samir: any limitations on retention for aggregated metrics vs raw traces?
[12:51] Jordan: metrics are cheaper; default retention is 1 year for rolled-up metrics, raw traces default 90 days. enterprise can extend both.
[13:03] Elena: let's talk about the pricing implications of running traces — how expensive is this?
[13:08] Jordan: trace capture pricing is usage-based; we bill per captured request and per GB stored. for a pilot we typically offer a credit. the Optimize view helps you estimate costs by giving per-request storage and projected monthly totals.
[13:22] Priya: also, sampling strategies can reduce cost a lot — 1% full capture plus rule-based capture for failures often sufficient to find root causes.
[13:32] Samir: that sounds reasonable.
[13:34] — priya walks through a specific failure example —
[14:10] Priya: (screen) here we have per-token latency overlay, you can see a token cluster at 1.8s — clicking it shows a kernel stall due to memory paging.
[14:22] Priya: we also annotate 'GC' events for our runtime when certain memory thresholds are crossed.
[14:30] Marcus: can we set alerts for kernel stalls?
[14:33] Priya: yes, alert on event types including GC, PAGE_FAULT, OOM.
[14:40] Elena: is runtime instrumentation open source or closed? we prefer agent visibility.
[14:44] Priya: parts are open — the telemetry agent and SDKs are open-source; the optimized kerns are proprietary.
[14:52] Samir: okay. for next steps i want a short list: security docs, sample tokenization diffs, pricing, and bench endpoints.
[14:59] Jordan: yea we'll get that over. Priya — anything else?
[15:04] Priya: i'll also prepare a short how-to for using the 'stitch mode' and an export template for logs.
[15:10] Elena: can you include a one-page diagram for how data flows in Private vs Hosted? IT will ask.
[15:16] Jordan: yes — we'll include a network diagram and deployment options.
[15:20] Samir: excellent.
[15:22] Marcus: two last quick Qs — is there an SLA credit for p95 misses? and what's the support model?
[15:28] Jordan: SLA credits are part of enterprise Dedicated contracts; support levels range from standard business hours to 24/7 platinum with phone on-call.
[15:38] Samir: sounds good.
[15:40] Priya: wrapping up — i'll note the action items: upload logs, send docs, schedule POC.
[15:46] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and the shared spreadsheet.
[15:50] Samir: thanks all.

[End of recording — total ~42 minutes]

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription mislabels some technical terms (e.g., KV cache -> K-V cash, VPC -> V-P-C). Speaker overlaps minimal. Some code/names obfuscated by noise.
